faq.eyebrow: A few things you might be wondering
faq.title: Good questions. Clear answers.

app.question: Is the DiskPond app free?
app.answer: Yes. The desktop app is free and open source under AGPL-3.0. You can use your own storage without a DiskPond account. DiskPond Cloud is a separate, upcoming paid storage service.

app.question: Where do my backups go?
app.answer: You choose the destination: a local or external drive, a mounted NAS, or a supported storage service. DiskPond Cloud will offer an optional managed destination when it launches.

app.question: Who can read my backed-up files?
app.answer: DiskPond encrypts backup contents on your device using your vault’s encryption password. Keep that password somewhere recoverable: DiskPond cannot reset it to unlock an existing vault.

app.question: How is this different from cloud sync?
app.answer: Sync keeps working files aligned across devices. Backup keeps separate, point-in-time versions that you can restore. Some sync providers also offer version history, but their retention and recovery limits vary.

app.question: What if I lose my computer?
app.answer: If your backup destination is still accessible and you have its credentials and encryption password, you can connect the vault from another supported Windows installation and restore your files.

app.question: Does DiskPond work on macOS or Linux?
app.answer: Windows 10 and 11 on x64 are the current release platform. macOS and Linux delivery are planned; downloads for those platforms are not available yet.

cloud.question: Can I buy DiskPond Cloud today?
cloud.answer: The service is coming soon. You can enquire about a personal or enterprise plan by email. The website does not take payments or provision storage yet; we’ll confirm availability before any purchase.

cloud.question: How does annual billing work?
cloud.answer: The 500 GB plan is €5 per month including VAT. The annual offer is 25% less than twelve monthly payments: €45 billed yearly, equivalent to €3.75 per month. VAT is included in both prices.

cloud.question: Do I have to use DiskPond Cloud?
cloud.answer: No. The free desktop app supports your own storage. The planned cloud service is an optional managed destination.

cloud.question: Where will the cloud storage be hosted?
cloud.answer: Hosting regions and the service’s availability, retention and recovery terms will be published before launch. Contact sales if you have location or business requirements.

cloud.question: Can you help with a larger deployment?
cloud.answer: Yes, you can discuss a tailored enterprise proposal with our sales team. Tell us your storage needs, device count and any support or deployment requirements so we can discuss the right fit.

guides.eyebrow: A little know-how goes a long way
guides.title: Make your backup a good one.
guides.description: Short, practical guides to getting set up and getting your files back.

items.title: Your first backup with DiskPond
items.description: From choosing a destination to checking your first restore.

sections.title: 1. Choose where the copy belongs
paragraphs: Install DiskPond on Windows 10 or 11 x64. Choose a storage destination that you can access: an external drive, a mounted network drive, or a supported storage provider.
A copy on the same physical drive won’t protect against that drive failing. For important files, keep an independent copy on another device and a copy off-site.

sections.title: 2. Create an encrypted vault
paragraphs: Choose Create a new vault, select the storage type and enter its connection details. Give the vault a name and choose an encryption password.

Store the password somewhere recoverable. You need it to reconnect to the vault; DiskPond cannot reset it to decrypt your backups. If you already have a compatible vault, use Connect an existing vault instead.

sections.title: 3. Add files and run a backup
paragraphs: Add a file or folder, then start a backup. Wait for its terminal result and review any reported issues. A connected vault or a running task is not proof that your files have been backed up.

Once the first backup completes, choose a schedule and retention settings that match how often your files change. Scheduled work requires DiskPond to be open or running in the tray, with the destination available.

sections.title: 4. Try a restore
paragraphs: Open the folder’s backup history, select a backup and browse its contents. Restore a test file into a new, empty folder and open it to check the result.
Repeat a small restore check occasionally, especially after changing storage or moving to another computer.

items.title: Find your files. Bring them back.
items.description: Recover a file, a folder, or an earlier version without the guesswork.

sections.title: Reconnect to your backup
paragraphs: Make sure your destination is available. On a new Windows installation, connect the existing vault using its storage credentials and encryption password. Do not create a new vault over the existing one.

sections.title: Choose the right moment
paragraphs: Open the source’s backup history and pick a version from before the change you want to undo. You can compare two backups to inspect added, changed and deleted paths, along with available size and modification metadata.
The Activity calendar shows retained backup history. It is not a complete log of every failed or canceled attempt, and versions removed by retention won’t remain available to restore.

sections.title: Restore into a fresh destination
paragraphs: Select the file, items or folder to restore. Prefer a new, empty destination so you can check the result before replacing a working copy. Review conflict options carefully when restoring into an existing folder.
Wait for the final result. Completed, partial, failed and canceled operations mean different things. Review any skipped files or errors, and open the restored files to confirm what you recovered.

sections.title: If something is unavailable
paragraphs: Reconnect an external drive or network share, check your storage credentials, and retry. Keep the original backup repository intact while investigating. Contact support with the error message, but never send passwords or provider secret keys.

items.title: Cloud sync and backup: better together
items.description: They solve different problems. Here’s where each fits.

sections.title: Sync is for the files you’re working on
paragraphs: Sync services keep current files aligned across devices and help with sharing and collaboration. Changes, including deletions, can propagate to other connected devices.
Many sync services offer trash recovery and version history. Their time limits, account requirements and recovery features vary, so check the terms of the service you use.

sections.title: Backup is a separate recovery history
paragraphs: A versioned backup saves point-in-time copies. You decide where those backups live and how long to retain them, then restore a selected version when needed.
DiskPond backs up files and folders. It is not a live synchronization service, a full-disk image, or a bare-metal system recovery tool.

sections.title: Think in independent copies
paragraphs: The 3-2-1 approach is a useful starting point: three copies, on two types of storage, with one copy off-site. The right setup depends on the value of your data and the failures you want to recover from.

An always-connected writable destination can still be affected by malware or compromised credentials. Consider a disconnected copy or provider-specific immutability where appropriate; do not assume encryption alone makes a backup immune to deletion.

sections.title: Test the way back
paragraphs: Whatever tools you choose, periodically restore a few files into a separate folder. Keep encryption passwords and storage recovery information somewhere you can reach if your main computer is lost.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.intro: A straightforward overview of this website and the DiskPond app.

sections.title: This website
sections.body: The site includes no analytics, advertising trackers or automatic crash-reporting scripts. Fonts and images are served with the site. Your appearance preference is saved in your browser’s local storage when you change it.

sections.title: Contacting us
sections.body: Contact links and the message composer open your own email app. The website does not collect or store form submissions. If you send an email, we receive the information you choose to share so we can respond. Do not include vault passwords or secret keys.

sections.title: Hosting and external services
sections.body: The hosting provider may process normal request information such as IP addresses and request logs to deliver the site. Downloads, source code and issue tracking are hosted on GitHub. Following an external link takes you to a service with its own privacy practices.

sections.title: The desktop app
sections.body: The desktop app does not send analytics or automatic crash reports. It communicates with your selected storage destinations and, when enabled, the update service. Diagnostics are local and exported by your action.

sections.title: Upcoming cloud storage
sections.body: DiskPond Cloud is not taking purchases through this site yet. Service-specific information about the operator, hosting, account data, retention and data-processing terms will be published before cloud signup opens.

terms.title: Website & software terms
terms.intro: The current website introduces DiskPond and its upcoming cloud offering.

sections.title: Open-source software
sections.body: The DiskPond desktop application is offered under AGPL-3.0. Its Kopia-derived core has a separate Apache-2.0 license. The applicable licenses, notices and source code are available in the project repository and release assets. Those licenses govern use and redistribution of the software.

sections.title: Cloud pricing and enquiries
sections.body: The announced 500 GB cloud plan is €5 per month including VAT, or €45 billed yearly under the 25% annual offer. Enterprise pricing is by proposal. The service is coming soon; an email enquiry is not a purchase, subscription, storage allocation or payment.

sections.title: Before cloud sales open
sections.body: The seller’s business details and service-specific terms, including availability, billing, renewal, cancellation, refunds and data handling, must be provided before an order is accepted. This website does not currently offer a checkout or customer account.

sections.title: Your backups
sections.body: Choose storage and retention appropriate to your needs, protect your encryption passwords, and check that your backups can be restored. The desktop app’s software licenses include their own warranty and liability terms.

sections.title: Credits
sections.body: DiskPond is derived from BlinkDisk and uses a Kopia-derived backup engine. Project and dependency licenses and notices remain with their respective contributors. The DiskPond service is independently operated.
